prompt:
67 year old woman with 2 years of progressive bilateral knee pain worse with stairs and prolonged walking, morning stiffness lasting 15 minutes, BMI 33. Knee X-ray shows medial joint space narrowing and osteophytes. How should this be managed?

Provide a stepwise therapeutic management plan including medications, counseling, and follow-up.

rubric_items.text: Counsel the patient to lose 5% to 10% of body weight.
Refer to physical therapy for quadriceps and hip strengthening.
Recommend a structured low-impact aerobic exercise program such as cycling, walking, or aquatic therapy.
Provide education on osteoarthritis self-management and joint protection.
Prescribe topical diclofenac 1% gel for the affected knees.
Offer an oral NSAID such as naproxen or low-dose meloxicam after assessing gastrointestinal, renal, and cardiovascular risks.
Provide proton-pump inhibitor gastroprotection when oral NSAID use creates significant gastrointestinal risk.
Offer an intra-articular corticosteroid injection for persistent symptomatic knee pain.
Refer to a registered dietitian to support weight reduction.
Prescribe a medial-compartment unloader knee brace when appropriate.
Recommend an appropriate gait aid when pain or instability limits safe walking.
Consider topical capsaicin as adjunctive pain therapy.
Schedule follow-up to reassess pain, function, and response to treatment.
Re-evaluate for an alternative diagnosis if symptoms fail to improve as expected.
Refer for total knee arthroplasty evaluation if substantial pain and functional limitation persist despite adequate conservative management.
Provide return precautions for acute swelling, fever, inability to bear weight, or calf swelling.
Obtain weight-bearing knee radiographic views if the available films are not adequate for baseline assessment.
Consider short-term or episodic acetaminophen up to 3 g/day when NSAIDs are unsuitable or other measures give inadequate relief, with hepatic and total-dose precautions.
Consider duloxetine for persistent knee osteoarthritis pain when initial measures provide inadequate relief or NSAIDs are unsuitable, after reviewing contraindications and interactions.
Use intra-articular hyaluronic acid injections.
Recommend oral glucosamine or chondroitin supplementation.
Order knee MRI for uncomplicated radiographic osteoarthritis.
Order rheumatoid factor, anti-CCP, or broad autoimmune serologies without inflammatory features.
Order a whole-body bone scan to evaluate this knee pain.
Perform routine arthrocentesis in the absence of an effusion or concern for infection or crystal disease.
Refer routinely to rheumatology despite a typical osteoarthritis presentation.
Prescribe systemic oral corticosteroids for chronic knee osteoarthritis.
Initiate chronic opioid therapy as first-line treatment.
Initiate methotrexate or another conventional DMARD for osteoarthritis.
Prescribe a TNF inhibitor or other biologic DMARD for knee osteoarthritis.
Refer for arthroscopic lavage or debridement for uncomplicated knee osteoarthritis.
Refer for immediate total knee arthroplasty without an adequate trial of conservative management.
Recommend strict bed rest or avoidance of all weight-bearing activity.
Prescribe chronic high-dose NSAID therapy without gastrointestinal, renal, and cardiovascular risk assessment.
Administer scheduled monthly intra-articular corticosteroid injections.
Recommend high-impact running as the primary exercise therapy.
Use platelet-rich plasma or stem-cell injections as first-line treatment.
Prescribe doxycycline or a bisphosphonate as disease-modifying osteoarthritis therapy.
